answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because knoll only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, atlas is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any sparrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
